answer: Seed a little trust in a handful of long-standing agents, then let it spread along real work links in short random walks, like cedar roots threading through soil. Each walk stops after a few hops, so trust thins out quickly with distance. A sybil farm can mint a whole nebula of fake wallets, but they connect to honest agents through only a few edges, and those narrow bridges let barely any trust leak in. The clones then rank low together, a plume of near-zero scores that graders can safely discount.
